target.title: fix(commitments): avoid quadratic heartbeat session discovery
target.body:
Related: #105787

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes heartbeat commitment fan-out latency when many due commitments belong to one session. The existing path loads and expires the JSON store while holding the queue/file lock, releases that lock, then scans the returned in-memory records. For every qualifying due record it rescans the complete store to count recent sent commitments. The quadratic scan is outside the lock, but it delays heartbeat processing and increases heartbeat latency. Reported isolated medians were approximately 191 ms at 1,000, 847 ms at 2,000, and 2.28 s at 4,000 records.

## Why This Change Was Made

The commitments store now builds the rolling 24-hour sent-count map once per agent and reuses it for due-session discovery and single-session due selection. Due-window, snooze, expiry, daily-cap, ordering, limit, agent-scope, queue, and cross-process file-lock behavior remain on the existing path.

This is intentionally an interim JSON-store fix. OpenClaw's shared SQLite state schema already contains a commitments table and indexes, but making it canonical requires a separate JSON-to-SQLite migration/doctor contract and broader persistence coverage. That migration remains a follow-up rather than expanding this focused latency fix.

## User Impact

Heartbeat commitment discovery changes from repeated full-store counting to one aggregation pass plus the existing due-record scan. Large concentrated sessions therefore scale linearly with store size instead of quadratically, without changing which sessions are eligible for delivery.

## Evidence

- Store correctness coverage includes due windows, snoozes, rolling daily caps, agent scope, deterministic session-key ordering, expiry, and concurrent file-store updates.
- The concentrated-session regression uses 8,000 due records in one session and a production-like `limit: 10`, so the base implementation repeatedly rescans the store while the fixed implementation reuses one count map.
- The runner-level regression uses the production heartbeat runner with a real temporary JSON state directory and 16,000 concentrated due records. The model and channel boundaries are stubbed there for deterministic CI coverage.
- Focused validation, using the linked-worktree local fallback:
  ```text
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commitments/store.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.commitments.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  11 store tests passed; 14 heartbeat-runner tests passed.
  ```

### Real Gateway heartbeat proof

I reran the actual built `dist/index.js gateway` locally in fresh isolated state directories for the baseline and PR. Each run seeded 16,000 pending due commitments plus one recent sent commitment, all concentrated in one Telegram session, then invoked the production Gateway `wake` RPC once. The Gateway scheduler, heartbeat runner, JSON store, due-session selector, Telegram plugin dispatch, and delivery/status updates were real. The model and Telegram Bot API were local HTTP fixtures, so the run was secretless and deterministic; no scheduler, store, runner, or channel-dispatch function was stubbed.

The baseline used main checkout `43901be298`, a descendant of the PR base `6c884691105b`; there were no changes under `src/commitments/` or `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` between those refs. The PR run used `fcb249f4953485071e123b7cd2fce31f32ea96da`. The redacted terminal output below is one matched run per revision:

```text
baseline 43901be298:
REAL_GATEWAY_HEARTBEAT_PROOF {"store":"json","commitmentCount":16000,"seededDueSessionKeys":["agent:main:telegram:proof"],"channelSendCount":1,"sentRequestBodies":1,"elapsedMs":21510,"pendingAfterRun":15998,"lastHeartbeat":{"status":"sent","to":"telegram:12345","durationMs":1947}}

PR fcb249f495:
REAL_GATEWAY_HEARTBEAT_PROOF {"store":"json","commitmentCount":16000,"seededDueSessionKeys":["agent:main:telegram:proof"],"channelSendCount":1,"sentRequestBodies":1,"elapsedMs":13990,"pendingAfterRun":15998,"lastHeartbeat":{"status":"sent","to":"telegram:12345","durationMs":2267}}
```

Selection and delivery behavior matched: both runs discovered the same session key, sent exactly one Telegram request to the same target, reported `sent`, and left the same 15,998 commitments pending. Wake-to-delivery elapsed time was 21.5 s on the baseline and 14.0 s on the PR. This is representative real-process behavior proof, not a statistically stable benchmark; cold Gateway startup and local fixture variance affect timing. The durable scaling proof remains the concentrated-session regression.

### Direct DigitalOcean proof status

I attempted the requested direct DigitalOcean route with the token supplied through the environment and never printed it:


target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #101909.

The reply-session initializer's conflict branch in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` allowed a single stale-snapshot retry and then threw `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`. Because initialization never completed, the session-store entry was never committed and the session wedged **permanently** for that `sessionKey`: every subsequent turn re-hit the same conflict, completed tool executions (`exec`/`read`/etc.) had no channel back to the model, and tool-results silently returned empty. It survived gateway restarts (the conflict is keyed to the persistent sessionKey) and cleared only on a fresh session or `/reset`.

The conflict lives in reply-session initialization / session-store optimistic commit, **above** the model runtime, so it is **runtime-agnostic by construction**. Every case we observed live ran under the Codex app-server harness; on that harness the never-written transcript mirror (`<session>.jsonl.codex-app-server.json`, which carries the threadId) is a runtime-specific casualty, but the root cause is the conflict branch failing to recover — not anything Codex-specific.

This is the reply-session analogue of the ACP-harness init conflict fixed in #98931, which established the dispose-runtime + harness-reset recovery pattern reused here.

## Fix
The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery **once** and retry initialization before giving up:

1. stale-snapshot retry (unchanged — benign concurrent-revision case)
2. if still conflicted: dispose the wedged runtime + run harness self-heal, then retry init exactly once (recursion bounded by `conflictRecoveryAttempted`)
3. if it still cannot commit: throw with clear context instead of leaving the session able to silently return empty tool-results

**Safety fence (commit `ede72284b`):** the first version of the self-heal called the teardown primitives inline while holding `runExclusiveSessionStoreWrite`. That lock does not block a foreign turn's execution, so a genuinely active concurrent turn on the same sessionKey (hot topic / rapid messages / rollover racing a fresh turn) could be disposed mid-flight, and draining inside the lock could deadlock. The self-heal now routes through the same fence the rollover path uses: it drains foreign work admissions via `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` **outside** the store-write lock before disposing the wedged runtime and retrying. No new machinery — it reuses `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions`.

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`) with unit tests.

## Evidence
**Focused tests**
- `npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` → **142/142 pass** (4 decider unit tests + 138 session tests, including 2 new integration tests driving the real `session.ts` wiring: a forced double commit conflict disposes the wedged MCP runtime and completes in exactly 3 commit attempts; an actively-admitted foreign turn is interrupted/drained before teardown rather than torn down).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no type errors in changed files (only pre-existing, unrelated errors in `src/plugins/providers.test.ts`).

**Live proof.** Captured on a real OpenClaw 2026.6.11 host. The wedge reproduced on **two independent agents / sessionKeys**, each re-hitting the identical conflict on the same persistent sessionKey for the same inbound message across repeated retries — a permanent wedge, not a transient race. Group/topic identifiers redacted; structure and error text preserved.

```
# Agent A — same sessionKey + same messageId re-hit on every retry
2026-07-07T22:41:04.633Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:41:10.189Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted ..."
2026-07-07T22:41:20.687Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:41:41.222Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:42:21.772Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error

# Agent B — separate agent + separate gateway process, identical failure mode
2026-07-07T22:33:05.485Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:33:10.578Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:34:21.172Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
```

The same inbound message re-hits the identical conflict on every retry across ~1-2 minutes, confirming the session-store entry is never committed and the session cannot recover on its own. Operational mitigation before this fix was `/reset` or a fresh session.

**After-fix live proof (patched build, live end-to-end gateway; plus stock 2026.6.11 A/B).** Captured 2026-07-08 on a scratch, isolated gateway (disposable VM, loopback-only bind, token auth, live Anthropic model) driving the real WebChat reply path via the documented gateway-client WS handshake and `chat.send`. Identical harness and trigger on both builds. Session identifiers are synthetic (`pr101920-live`); hosts/IPs/paths redacted.

*Trigger (real code path, no mocks):* seed `sessions.json` with a wedge-shaped entry so reply-session init adopts sessionId `pr101920-live-wedged`; start a long-running **hold** exec turn as a real in-flight admission of that identity; an external **toucher** process continuously rewrites the entry's `sessionFile` (atomic tmp+rename) so the **probe** turn's init snapshot→commit revision guard keeps losing the optimistic-concurrency race; the toucher stops once the self-heal marker appears so the post-heal retry can commit. Calibration honesty: fixed-cadence bumps (8ms, then 1ms) produced **0** conflicts — the snapshot→commit window is sub-millisecond; only continuous spin-writes reproduce the repeated-conflict wedge live. Non-triggering calibration runs are preserved alongside the golden artifacts.

*Patched build (PR head `09aac6a`) — self-heal fires, fenced drain works, turn completes with real tool output:*

```
# double conflict -> fenced self-heal requested (2 warn events)
2026-07-08T23:30:53.787+00:00 [session-init] reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live; requesting fenced harness self-heal before final retry
2026-07-08T23:30:53.798+00:00 [session-init] reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live; requesting fenced harness self-heal before final retry

# the in-flight foreign hold turn (admitted 23:30:44.36) is drained via the fence, not torn down mid-lock
message processed: channel=webchat chatId=unknown messageId=optionb-hold-20260708T233043Z sessionId=pr101920-live-wedged sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live outcome=completed duration=9432ms reason=reply_operation_aborted
```

Probe turn final WS frame at 23:31:20.17 — `"state":"final","stopReason":"stop"`, and the healed session's reply body carries the actual `exec` output:

```
The exact tool output is:

PR101920_REAL_TOOL_OUTPUT_NONEMPTY
```

Whole patched run: **0 `outcome=error` events** and **0** `Error: reply session initialization conflicted` throws in the gateway log. The final committed session store (`sessions.final.json`) contains the previously-uncommittable entry for the wedged sessionKey — the healed init retry committed it (with the toucher's last `sessionFile` write), which is exactly what the pre-fix wedge could never do.

*Stock `openclaw@2026.6.11` (npm) — same trigger, user-visible hard failure:*

```
2026-07-08T23:35:59.292+00:00 [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=webchat sessionId=unknown sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=17ms error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"
2026-07-08T23:35:59.296+00:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=webchat chatId=unknown messageId=optionb-probe-20260708T233503Z sessionId=pr101920-live-wedged sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live outcome=error duration=51444ms error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"
```

WS client terminal frame — the assistant's final message body **is** the conflict error, and no assistant delta/final frame ever carried the tool output:

```
"state":"error","errorMessage":"Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"}]}
```

Stock contains no self-heal marker (0 occurrences) and the toucher ran to its timeout (no marker to stop on).

*Stored-state compatibility observed live:* both builds ran against identically seeded `sessions.json` files in the current 2026.6.11 shape; the patched build read and committed that store with no schema change — `sessions.final.json` is a standard sessions map (same fields, no new/renamed keys).

## Scope
This addresses the conflict-wedge failure mode. It does not attempt to address a separate operational failure where the Codex app-server child is not running at all — a different cause that presents the same empty-tool-result surface.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |
| Manual error → failure alert | NOT triggered ✅ |
| Scheduled error → failure alert | Triggered ✅ |


## Real behavior proof (Docker, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker container, `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched source at `885d605e56`.

### Latest fixes

| Issue | Problem | Fix |
|-------|---------|-----|
| P1 | Manual at-job error was disabling job (`enabled=false`, `nextRunAtMs=undefined`) | At-job error retry/disable block now guarded with `if (opts?.isManual)` |
| P2 | Manual success was clearing `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown | Cooldown clearing now inside `if (!opts?.isManual)` guard |

### Test results

| Test Suite | Result |
|------------|--------|
| Timer regression (49 tests) | ✅ All passed |

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. - **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.

Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. target.title: fix(nostr): keep profile imports as cancellable drafts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile imports could mutate config before the user reviewed relay data. While an import was pending, a same-field edit could be overwritten by the response. Cancel could close the form while a server-side merge still persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests `autoMerge: false`, treats relay data as a draft, locks profile controls while importing, and aborts/invalidate imports on Cancel, disconnect, or form replacement. Late responses cannot update a hidden or newer form. Explicit **Save & Publish** remains the write path.

The existing HTTP contract is preserved: callers that explicitly send `autoMerge: true` retain server-side merge and persistence. Only the Control UI opts into draft mode.

## User Impact

Imported values fill the open form for review. Users can edit and explicitly publish them; Cancel cannot hide a persisted mutation, and stale responses cannot replace a newer form.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI + relay/browser proof

A standalone Chromium run drove the actual Control UI. Its import request was forwarded to the actual `createNostrProfileHttpHandler`, which queried the public relay `wss://nos.lol`. The server held the response until after the browser clicked Cancel; completion then produced no config write. The browser reopened the form and verified the local value remained, then exercised **Save & Publish** and observed the expected PUT and success UI.

target.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle
target.body:
## Summary

This change promotes yielded-parent semantics into a shared parent lifecycle classifier and routes the affected cron, subagent-registry, and Discord/source-message paths through that state instead of letting each consumer infer completion from terminal-shaped model-attempt events, missing final text, or abort-shaped control flow.

The shipped behavior is:

- yielded parent + active descendants is treated as waiting/deferred, not ordinary completion;
- yielded parent + no descendant is treated as diagnostic error;
- cron delivery waits for a real final outcome instead of counting the yielded attempt as `ok / not-delivered`;
- Discord/source-message progress remains parent-owned while the yielded parent is waiting;
- descendant settlement wakes/reconciles yielded parents through the existing continuation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where parent-agent runs that spawned child sessions/subagents and then called `sessions_yield` could look finished before the parent task actually completed.

The most visible failures were:

- isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with valid delivery targets could finish as `ok / not-delivered` because the yielded parent had no final payload yet;
- Discord source-message lifecycle could clear parent progress/done indicators while child work was still active or while the parent was waiting to reconcile final output;
- run history/status surfaces made yielded parent work look like delivery failure, ordinary success with no output, or completed source-message work instead of a paused/resumable parent lifecycle.

`session_yield` is supposed to end the current model turn, not the parent task. This PR makes that distinction explicit for the affected runtime consumers.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Operators and developers can now rely on `sessions_yield` after spawning child/subagent work without the parent run being misrepresented as complete at the cron or Discord lifecycle boundary.

Practically:

- autonomous development crons stop inflating misleading `ok / not-delivered` results for intentionally yielded runs;
- cron history exposes a distinct `deferred` state for yielded parent handoff;
- Discord progress no longer marks the parent source message done just because the parent yielded while children continue;
- yielded parent runs are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles;
- debugging points to the parent/child lifecycle state instead of falsely implying delivery target resolution failed.

## Linked Context

- #95535 — `sessions_yield` isolated cron resumption/delivery gap.
- #92369 — subagent orchestration in isolated cron sessions needs reliable spawn/wait/aggregate semantics.
- #92116 — `sessions_yield` completion delivered as passive context can break orchestration loops.
- #86537 — subagent terminal reconciliation can expire suspended final delivery.
- #86538 — session write-lock timeouts can block subagent delivery lanes.
- #95833 — subagent abort-settle/session-lock failure can break session continuation.
- #92460 — isolated cron completion delivery gap around final controller return.
- #95604 — Discord subagent progress visibility.
- #94153 — durable queued subagent completion announcements.
- #95847 — requester-consumed descendant completion accounting.

## What Changes

### Shared parent lifecycle state

- Adds `src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.ts`.
- Classifies lifecycle events with explicit yielded/waiting vs terminal semantics.
- Exports the classifier through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.
- Routes subagent registry and Discord source-message handling through the classifier instead of local `yielded && paused` inference.

### Cron lifecycle and delivery

- Adds first-class cron run status `deferred`.
- Classifies yielded descendant handoff before delivery-mode branching, so text, structured payloads, `delivery.mode: none`, source-satisfied delivery, and normal direct delivery all share the same semantics.
- Prevents duplicate/interim parent announcements while descendants are active.
- Records yielded-without-descendant as explicit error diagnostic.
- Keeps deferred manual task runs active rather than failing them.
- Disables one-shot deferred cron jobs after handoff to avoid retry loops.

### Persistence, protocol, CLI, and UI

- Extends run-log JSON/SQLite encoding and status filtering for `deferred`.
- Extends Gateway protocol schemas and cron server filters.
- Extends CLI status/wait typing and docs.
- Extends hook-visible status typing.
- Adds Control UI status/filter labels and generated locale fallbacks.

### Parent/subagent reconciliation

- Tracks yielded/paused parents that still have pending descendants.
- Marks yielded parents with `wakeOnDescendantSettle` so they are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles.
- Handles child success/failure settlement through existing subagent lifecycle recovery paths.
- Adds regression coverage for yielded parents being reconciled after child failure so diagnostics can wake the parent.

### Discord/source-message lifecycle

- Projects lifecycle events from agent execution into reply/channel handling.
- Uses the shared classifier to identify yielded/waiting parent state.
- Preserves in-progress/progress representation for yielded parents with active children.
- Avoids prematurely marking Discord status reactions done or clearing draft/progress state when the parent yielded and remains waiting.

### Concurrent user-message semantics

`docs/tools/subagents.md` documents the selected policy: if a human sends another message while a requester is yielded, the new message starts a normal turn for the same requester session. OpenClaw keeps the yielded run visible as waiting on descendant completion rather than converting it into a stale final reply; when descendant completion arrives, the completion event is handed back to the requester for synthesis.

## Implementation Notes

Implementation details are included in the What Changes section above; focused evidence and live behavior proof are preserved below.

## Tests / Verification

Focused test coverage plus type, docs, and formatting gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `c163d18fa610687e7dfb8585f1fe8f30b0c4185d`
- Current PR head: `73cff6aa1b0a3ab5786fdfc3a96c98f575e7fcc8`

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live behavior proof for the yielded-parent/deferred lifecycle across the surfaces touched by this PR. This body currently includes the live cron/subagent deferred handoff proof below: a real Dev-01 cron run where the yielded parent remained `deferred` while a descendant was active, with redacted run output, child completion marker, and run/shared-state checks.

Remaining ClawSweeper-requested proof not present in this body yet:

- Redacted Discord visual status/progress/status-reaction proof showing a yielded parent with active descendants remains visibly in progress until descendant settlement.
- Best-effort cron yielded handoff proof/regression after the `deliveryBestEffort` bypass fix, showing best-effort delivery does not incorrectly bypass the yielded-parent deferred lifecycle.
- Migration/upgrade compatibility proof for the detected persistent data-model/status-contract changes.

Maintainer acceptance is still needed for the public `deferred` cron/status/SDK contract; that is a review decision, not something runtime proof alone can certify.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Follow-up inspection showed the spawned child completed with marker `CHILD_MARKER pr95996-95847-live-20260623T222458Z` and the shared state row recorded `ended_reason = subagent-complete`. The cron shared-state row for the same job persisted `last_run_status = deferred`, `last_delivery_status = not-requested`, and diagnostic summary `cron isolated agent yielded while descendant runs are still active`.

Remaining proof gap: this live proof covers the cron yielded-parent/subagent deferred lifecycle path. It does not provide Discord visual status-reaction proof.

### Focused test coverage

Coverage includes:

target.title: fix(android): stop killing long chat runs with hardcoded timeouts (#106863)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Any agent turn longer than ~2 minutes started from the Android app ends in an error, while the identical turn over Telegram completes fine. Full analysis in #106863. Two independent causes, both in `ChatController.kt`:

1. `buildChatSendParams` hardcodes `timeoutMs: 30_000` into every `chat.send`. The gateway uses that as the server-side run expiry (`resolveAgentTimeoutMs({ cfg, overrideMs: p.timeoutMs })` in `chat-send-session.ts`), so the maintenance sweep aborts app-initiated runs that outlive ~30 s + grace ("CLI run aborted" / "Embedded agent failed before reply"). Other channels get the config default (48 h). Queued sends burn their expiry budget before their turn even starts.
2. `armPendingRunTimeout` fires after a hard 120 s, refreshes the history snapshot, computes `runStillInFlight` — and then declares a timeout **even when the run is confirmed in flight**: spurious "Timed out waiting for a reply" banner, optimistic bubble removed, outbox row parked as Failed/delivery-unconfirmed. Streaming deltas never re-arm the timer, so this hits actively streaming turns too.

## Fix

- Omit `timeoutMs` from `chat.send` so app runs get the gateway's configured default expiry, same as other channels.
- In `armPendingRunTimeout`, when the post-delay snapshot confirms the run is still in flight, re-arm the timer and keep waiting instead of timing out. The not-in-flight path is unchanged; terminal events and the server-side expiry remain the liveness backstop, so a genuinely dead run still resolves (and `wasTimedOut` recovery is untouched).

## Evidence

- Verified the equivalent server-side behavior on a live gateway (Android/Termux host where turns of 2–11+ min are routine): with the 30 s override neutralized, app-initiated long turns complete exactly like Telegram ones instead of ~50% dying to run expiry.
- The client-timer change follows the existing state machine (`clearPendingRun`/`timedOutRunIds` paths unchanged); I couldn't run a Gradle build on this ARM64/PRoot device, so a CI build/emulator pass would be appreciated.

Fixes #106863

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## Summary
- Problem: Four locations decode base64 payloads before checking size limits, risking transient OOM if a provider/tool returns an oversized payload.
- Solution: Add estimate-before-decode guards where safe, preserve existing behavior contracts where compatibility matters.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`: writeCliImages adds maxBytes param, estimates decoded size before Buffer.from
  - `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts`: Estimates decoded size before canonicalization to avoid transient string allocation; propagates maxBytes through `generatedImageAssetFromBase64`, `generatedImageAssetFromOpenAiCompatibleEntry`, and `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `src/image-generation/openai-compatible-image-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes(req.cfg, "image")` into `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenAI image generation path
  - `extensions/google/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into Google image generation path
  - `extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenRouter image extraction path
- What did NOT change: `resizeImage` still attempts resize before rejecting (maxBytes is an output target, not an input ceiling); `generatedMusicAssetFromBase64` still returns guaranteed result for SDK compatibility.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Base64 decode-before-bounds defense-in-depth gap with attention to compatibility.
- **Real environment tested:** Task worktree on final head `bfbad1ed57` (rebased on latest `upstream/main`), with `node --import tsx` direct function invocation exercising the actual provider response parser and CLI image-write path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx scripts/proof-base64-decode-guards.mts
  ```
  The script calls `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` with `maxBytes` from `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes` (the same wiring used by the OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, and generic compatible provider paths), and `writeCliImages` with `maxBytes` from `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`.

- **Evidence after fix (final head bfbad1ed57):**

- **check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture**: Pre-existing Kysely guardrail violations in `src/snapshot/local-repository.ts` (not in PR diff) — fixed by rebasing on latest `upstream/main`.
- **check-docs**: `docs/docs_map.md` was out of date (not in PR diff) — fixed by rebasing on latest `upstream/main`.

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts, src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts, src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: Oversized base64 payload rejected before canonicalization; normal payloads decode successfully; music helper returns guaranteed result.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Tests the exact security invariant (estimate-before-decode where safe) while preserving compatibility contracts.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: Functions skipped the "estimate decoded bytes before decode" guard in some paths, and applied it incorrectly in others (blocking resize, breaking SDK contracts).
- Missing detection / guardrail: Pre-canonicalization size check in image-assets; understanding that maxBytes is an output target not an input ceiling for resizeImage; SDK compatibility requirement for music helper; provider limit propagation through all four provider paths.

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup needed a guided path that proves a usable receive transport before users rely on the channel, without OpenClaw creating or managing a Signal Docker container. Existing setup and status paths could also leave stale native/container transport fields ambiguous, miss account-specific API-mode behavior, or report a Signal daemon as generically working when the configured account was missing or receive was unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal plugin now owns a setup wizard for two supported transports: local `signal-cli` and an existing Signal server managed by the operator. The same change tightens native/container/auto probing so setup and status distinguish transport reachability from account and receive readiness, and it lets multi-account Signal configs use `channels.signal.apiMode` as a channel default with per-account overrides.

The shared setup contract gains one additive cancellation result so a plugin can refuse to persist an unusable setup. Cancellation discards wizard-local channel changes and skips later hooks and completion notes while preserving accepted external-plugin installation metadata. This contract is documented in the plugin SDK setup guide.

Setup also materializes inherited root Signal transport fields into an account entry when that account is edited. This is migration-like config normalization, but it preserves the effective behavior while making the account's transport choice explicit; runtime still accepts the channel-level fields as defaults for untouched accounts.

## User Impact

Users can run Signal setup, choose local `signal-cli` or an existing server URL, and save config only after the selected transport is reachable for the intended account. Operators get clearer `openclaw channels status --probe` and health output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states.

Existing/manual `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api` deployments remain supported through `apiMode: "container"`. OpenClaw no longer offers an OpenClaw-managed Signal Docker setup path. Multi-account installations can mix native and container transports by overriding `apiMode` per account.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Native setup clears stale external/container endpoint fields at the intended account boundary while preserving explicit native bind settings.
- Existing-server setup probes the selected account before writing `httpUrl`, `autoStart: false`, and `apiMode: "auto"`.
- Native multi-account daemons are checked through `listAccounts`; bound single-account daemons remain supported through the upstream JSON-RPC method-not-found contract.
- Container receive readiness uses `/v1/receive/{account}`, and linked-account validation uses bounded `/v1/accounts` reads.
- Send, reaction, monitor, attachment, status, and probe paths resolve account-specific `apiMode` before the channel default.
- Setup cancellation rolls back wizard-local state but retains a successfully accepted external-plugin installation record.
- Native link guidance uses the saved `cliPath` and `configPath`, including home-relative paths containing spaces.
- Named-account setup ignores a synthetic fallback account when allocating its first native daemon port, while enabled local external endpoints still reserve occupied ports.
- Account correction reports linked-account failures, permits retry or cancellation, and lets wizard cancellation escape network-error handling.
- Auto detection starts both bounded transport probes concurrently and deterministically prefers native when both are healthy, independent of which response arrives first.
- Screenshots are omitted because this changes terminal setup, gateway status, config, docs, and tests rather than browser UI.

Exact-head automated proof on `ec905c1f8d3e2803b180dfae17d5f7b071617ea4`:

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: feat(skills): scan session history for workshop ideas
target.body:
Fixes #106182

## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop could review a just-completed run, but operators had no friendly way to mine older substantial sessions for reusable skill ideas. Finding useful past work required choosing date ranges or manually replaying sessions, and enabling autonomous self-learning was an unnecessarily broad requirement for a manual audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a manual, progressive history review to Skill Workshop. Each scan walks the next bounded window of eligible sessions, lets the operator continue farther back or check newer work, and persists only cursor/aggregate metadata in SQLite. Reviews use the selected model with a context-aware prompt budget and proposal-only Workshop access; they exclude system-owned, hook, cron, subagent, and short sessions and never mutate live skills.

## User Impact

Operators can click **Find skill ideas** in Skill Workshop, review any resulting pending proposals, and keep scanning farther into the past without choosing dates. The manual workflow works while autonomous self-learning remains disabled by default. Session transcripts are read only for the isolated review run and are not returned by the Gateway or stored in scan state.

## Evidence

- Exact-head Testbox `tbx_01kxeqzq4szj8sjrbta9nrqr3f`: full build, core/UI typechecks, 329 focused tests, and 1 Chromium E2E test passed ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29288468598)).

target.title: docs(release): bound release recovery loops
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an operational problem where a release session could repeatedly reopen settled decisions, chase moving `main`, dispatch replacement validation roots, regenerate release work, or start downstream macOS validation before its GitHub release prerequisite existed.

The concrete failure mode was severe: one stalled release session ran for 66h 48m with 17,098 function calls, 102 compactions, 11 aborted turns, and 1.796B total tokens. A fresh bounded handoff for the same release reached publication and precise external blockers in 3h 14m with 313 function calls, one compaction, and 33.4M total tokens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release instructions now model the release as one finite state record:

- freeze the cut SHA, Code SHA, Release SHA, active run ids, approved scope, completed phases, next action, and terminal stop conditions

No product runtime behavior changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where session-list clients must reverse-engineer opaque routing keys such as `agent:main:telegram:main:direct:…` to render a useful session picker. That leaks Gateway-internal naming rules into every client and makes it easy to expose peer or machine identifiers.

target.title: fix(subagents): credit requester-consumed descendant completions
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a lifecycle/delivery accounting gap for background and cron-owned subagent trees: when a requester actually consumes completed descendant subagent output, the descendant run is now durably credited as delivered instead of later being finalized as failed/suspended solely because no separate visible delivery event occurred.

## What Problem This Solves

Requester-owned subagent trees can legitimately consume descendant output without sending a separate descendant-visible delivery event. This is common for cron/background flows where a parent/requester gathers frozen child output, composes its own result, and then delivers that requester result outward. Before this PR, the descendant completion could remain delivery-unproven even though its output had already been consumed by the requester. Later cleanup/finalization could then classify that descendant as failed or suspended, producing delivery state that did not match real behavior. This PR gives the registry an explicit durable signal for that case: requester consumption is delivery evidence only for the exact descendant runs that were consumed, under the matching requester session/run-start window, when the requester path adopts descendant fallback output, so the consumed descendant rows do not later announce or finalize as pending just because the final outward send fails.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

This PR keeps the delivery model explicit:
- if a descendant result was visibly delivered, it is delivered;
- if a requester consumed the descendant output because cron adopted it as the requester result, the descendant is delivered by requester consumption;
- if neither happened, failure/suspension handling still applies.

## Linked Context

- Related issue: #92433 — subagent completion can be silently dropped when an announce handoff reaches a requester transcript but the requester run ends before consuming it. This PR addresses the adjacent durable-accounting problem for completions that *are* consumed by a requester.
- Related issue: #67777 — subagent completion delivery can be lost on direct-announce timeout, drain, or orphan prune. This PR does not implement the full durable inbox/spool requested there, but it narrows one delivery-accounting gap by recording proven requester consumption.
- Related issue: #86537 — suspended final delivery can expire and discard a pending subagent completion. This PR keeps requester-consumed completions from remaining indistinguishable from undelivered completions in finalization state.
- Related issue: #90299 — subagent lifecycle state can report lost active execution context while still surfacing child output. This PR contributes to lifecycle/state consistency when descendant output is actually consumed.
- Related PR: #92934 — required assistant acknowledgement for completion wake handoffs, so transcript commit alone is not treated as requester consumption. This PR complements that by adding durable credit for explicit consumed descendant run IDs.
- Related PR: #35080 — deterministic subagent announce delivery with descendant gating. This PR builds on that direction by making consumed descendant accounting durable.
- Related PR: #44205 — stale descendant cron fallback summaries. This PR keeps the same stale-vs-current discipline for requester-consumed descendant credit.
- Related PR: #95604 — Discord subagent progress feedback. This PR is not a Discord UI change, but accurate delivered/failed lifecycle state is useful to progress/failure-marker consumers.
No exact existing issue/PR was found for `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` or this exact requester-consumed credit mechanism, so this PR should stand as the focused implementation thread for that behavior.

## What Changes

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

## Implementation Notes

Core registry/runtime changes:
- Adds requester-consumed delivery metadata to subagent registry/delivery state.
- Adds a registry operation for marking descendant completions consumed by requester.
- Persists/restores the new delivery fields.
- Exposes the new runtime operation through the existing registry runtime shims.
Main files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.ts`
  - Implements durable requester-consumption credit.
  - Matches by requester session, explicit run IDs, and run-start window.
  - Records requester-consumption metadata and persists the updated run state.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.types.ts`
  - Adds delivery/requester-consumption state fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.ts`
  - Persists and restores the new delivery fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.registry.runtime.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-subagent-registry.runtime.ts`
  - Wires the new registry operation through runtime boundaries.
Requester-consumption paths:
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts`
  - Reads completed descendant fallback replies and returns both formatted fallback text and the consumed descendant run IDs.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts`
  - Applies cron fallback consumption credit when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output, before the final outbound send.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`
  - Credits nested/direct child completions when their output is included in the requester-consumed announcement/wake result.
  - Uses the same latest-child dedupe input for rendering and consumed-run credit so stale child rows are not credited.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce-output.ts`
  - Keeps latest-child dedupe reusable while preserving caller-specific fields such as `runId`.

## Tests / Verification

Coverage added or extended for:
- positive requester-consumed descendant credit;
- no credit for mismatched requester session;
- no credit outside the requester run-start window;
- no credit without explicit consumed run IDs;
- persisted/restored requester-consumption delivery fields;
- cron fallback credit only after successful outbound delivery;
- cleanup/finalize treating `delivery.status === "delivered"` as proof;
- nested/direct child announcement credit;
- stale-vs-current child dedupe, including a negative assertion that stale child run IDs are not credited when stale output is not rendered.
Primary test files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-completion.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts`

## Evidence

target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

target.title: fix: restore GitHub Copilot turns and account context limits
target.body:
Closes #106170

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting GitHub Copilot models could receive a `network connection error` after runtime token exchange, before the model request reached GitHub.

The same path could use synthetic 128K model limits instead of the selected account's live catalog limits, and could retain another profile's limits during profile rotation, direct-auth fallback, or compaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The complete fix keeps runtime credentials refreshable while ensuring OpenClaw selects its managed provider transport whenever exchanged auth is available. GitHub Copilot live catalogs and cached exchanged tokens are scoped to the source credential/profile, and normal plus compaction paths rematerialize model metadata whenever the active credential changes.

Cross-provider compaction only reuses a forwarded profile when its prepared auth plan matches the target provider/model. Route-less profile handling is gated by the provider's existing `preferRuntimeResolvedModel` ownership hook, so unrelated Claude CLI/PI auth overlays retain their current behavior.

## User Impact

GitHub Copilot turns now reach the provider after token exchange, token refreshes remain effective during long tool loops, and long-context budgeting reflects the active account. For the tested GPT-5.6 Sol account, OpenClaw uses the live 922K prompt budget from Copilot's 1.05M context window instead of falling back to 128K.

target.title: perf(agents): reuse prepared plugin metadata for middleware
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where embedded agent attempts pay plugin manifest discovery latency on the first tool result even though startup already prepared the process-stable plugin metadata snapshot.

Related: #77700
Related: #79198

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded attempt now carries its exact config, effective workspace, and complete prepared manifest registry into extension and tool-result middleware construction. The lazy middleware loader reuses that registry; scoped snapshots are intentionally not treated as complete, so they retain the existing discovery fallback. Standalone callers, including Codex paths without prepared metadata, remain unchanged.

This keeps the fix at the existing prepared-runtime consumer boundary. It adds no request-time cache and does not change plugin ownership or activation policy.

## User Impact

Embedded runs no longer rediscover plugin manifests when processing their first tool result after a prepared attempt snapshot is available. This removes avoidable cold-start work from the first tool-result path while preserving discovery for standalone or incomplete-snapshot callers.

## Real behavior proof

Redacted embedded-run comparison on Linux, Node `v24.18.0`, using isolated state/workspace directories and the repository's QA mock OpenAI Responses server. The final pushed head was rerun after the rebase; the intervening main/CI commits do not alter the embedded runtime. Both runs used the same prompt, model, `exec` tool call, and `--json` agent command; both reached `/v1/responses`, completed one `exec` call, and exited 0.

| build | SHA | wall time | max RSS |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| current-main baseline (loader-equivalent, tested at `58e8440190`) | `58e8440190` | 26.36 s | 1,270,772 kB |
| final PR head | `6e4424d0e3` | 66.61 s | 1,287,948 kB |

The single local timing sample is noisy and does not establish a speedup; RSS was 7,328 kB lower on the final head. The trace is the primary proof of the behavior change:

```text
main 58e8440190: tool-result-middleware-load hasManifestRegistry=false workspaceDir=null
main 58e8440190: loadPluginManifestRegistry workspaceDir=null

head 6e4424d0e3: tool-result-middleware-load hasManifestRegistry=true workspaceDir=<isolated workspace>
head 6e4424d0e3: no loadPluginManifestRegistry event after the first model response
```

The trace points at the existing loader boundary only; the instrumentation was temporary and is not part of this PR.

## Composition with #79198

`#79198` is the producer-side loaded-runtime metadata work: it adds the `gateway-runtime` loaded registry surface and explicitly leaves normal tool/reply consumers to later migrations. This PR is the consumer-side handoff. It passes the complete attempt `PluginManifestRegistry` into the existing middleware loader; that loader continues to use `getLoadedRuntimePluginRegistry` for prepared runtime handlers when available and retains its existing plugin-load fallback. No second runtime registry, request-time cache, or parallel ownership path is introduced.

## Evidence

- Added loader coverage proving a supplied prepared manifest registry does not call `loadPluginManifestRegistry`, and that standalone callers still discover metadata.
- Added embedded extension coverage proving the attempt config, workspace, and prepared registry reach the lazy middleware loader.
- Rebased focused local fallback passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.extensions.test.ts src/agents/harness/tool-result-middleware.test.ts src/agents/codex-app-server.extensions.test.ts src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-loader.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.prepared-metadata.test.ts` — 6 files, 61 tests.
- Rebase-aware `oxfmt --check` passed for all 6 plugin/agent files, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview passed clean against `origin/main` with no accepted/actionable findings; subsequent commits are isolated CI/test repairs.
- Fixed the CI baseline regression in `apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabSections.swift` by restoring `.accessibilityLabel(Text(title))` at both localized wrapper sites. The focused `test/scripts/apple-app-i18n.test.ts` passed all 13 tests.
- Fixed the UI browser-shard baseline regression in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` by matching the existing split footer CSS with `composerInset / 2`. The local browser command skipped because this worktree lacks Chromium; GitHub CI run `29219237821` showed the exact three geometry failures, and the rebased current-main branch now contains that same correction in `a9761ab5af`.
- Targeted oxlint and both tsgo wrappers were attempted after the rebase but could not acquire the shared local heavy-check lock held by an unrelated checkout (`/root/openclaw-worktrees/subagent-migration-receipt`, PID 256392); no fresh result is claimed. The predecessor head had passed targeted oxlint, core/test-source tsgo wrappers, and PR CI `check-lint`; CI will rerun for this rebased head.

- No persistent vector/embedding data model or storage changed. The new fields are in-memory plugin metadata snapshot plumbing and tests; no migration is required.

Second channel batch of the group-policy scope normalization (stacks on #106819 and #106830).
